purpose: Align historical static and browser contracts with the canonical Surface Standard runtime, and escalate any falsified runtime assumption into the effective standard rather than masking it in evidence consumers.

saturationImpact.reason: Historical alignment exposed one stable post-decision runtime vocabulary regression; later retained-browser failures are stale or internally contradictory evidence consumers and do not add runtime primitives.

invariants.name: semantic-token-declaration
invariants.rule: Historical design-system assurance validates --ds-ease: rather than the invalid --ds-ease;.

invariants.name: progressive-settings-sequencing
invariants.rule: Browser journeys fill organization while its disclosure is open, then open provider and fill provider fields.

invariants.name: progressive-job-sequencing
invariants.rule: Browser journeys open criteria and schedule groups before interacting with controls they own.

invariants.name: canonical-terminal-vocabulary
invariants.rule: Historical browser assertions consume Accetta nel catalogo, Accettata nel catalogo and Scarica evidenza.

invariants.name: no-runtime-bypass
invariants.rule: Alignment does not force hidden controls, disable single-open behavior, modify server authority, or reintroduce legacy labels.

invariants.name: same-head-evidence
invariants.rule: Historical-contract assurance, Surface Standard assurance, server-backed browser and general CI execute against the same PR head before maturity.

invariants.name: stable-post-toggle-observation
invariants.rule: Single-open assertions observe stable post-toggle state with bounded condition waiting, not instantaneous counts or arbitrary sleeps.

invariants.name: direct-rerender-terminal-reconciliation
invariants.rule: A source decision direct rerender emits ictc:surface-changed after DOM reconstruction so terminal layers reconcile stable DOM.

invariants.name: legacy-visual-journey-terminal-shell
invariants.rule: The retained Enterprise 1.8 visual journey asserts the current candidate terminal shell while preserving geometry, role, keyboard and overflow budgets.

invariants.name: scenario-actor-consistency
invariants.rule: A named role scenario must retain that actor until the scenario ends; the S01 auditor scenario cannot switch to user before asserting auditor title, status and disclosure order.

observedFailures.observation: design-system check expected --ds-ease; while runtime declares --ds-ease:...
product journey hid organization by opening provider before filling organization fields.
journey asserted instantaneous open count while toggle reconciliation was still closing a sibling.
renderSourceDialog rebuilt base vocabulary after refresh-time terminal reconciliation.
retained 1.8 journey asserted pre-candidate shell vocabulary and repeated old settings ordering.
S01 was initialized as auditor, immediately selected user, then asserted auditor title and Sola lettura state.

preventiveAlignments.reason: controls are interacted with through their current disclosure owner.
historical journeys consume canonical terminal copy so stable legacy regressions remain observable.
older-version visual journeys preserve invariant budgets while consuming current candidate shell.
role-labelled browser phases cannot mutate actor before role-specific assertions complete.

acceptance: Static token and historical contract checks pass without weakening production design tokens.
Product and retained Enterprise 1.8 journeys complete progressive settings flow.
The product journey completes progressive job flow and stable source decision vocabulary.
The retained Enterprise 1.8 journey keeps its geometry, least-privilege, keyboard, overflow and target-size budgets while consuming current shell copy.
S01 of the Enterprise 2 browser remains auditor from initialization through auditor-specific assertions; the first user transition occurs in S04.
No API permission, capability or backend authority is weakened.
Surface Standard assurance, server-backed UI-standard browser, all historical browser journeys, contract audit, runtime E2E and security are re-evaluated on the same final PR head.
claimBoundary: This model demonstrates historical-contract alignment and runtime corrections falsified by that alignment. It does not establish universal regression freedom, accessibility conformance, legal compliance, certification or production readiness.
